It’s a quiet evening at Piandao’s home. Toph and Katara are alone in the guest bedroom. There’s a cloying scent permeating every inch of this space, like a field of jasmine that’s been razed by a wildfire. Without comment, Katara goes to the window and flings it open, then lingers there, enjoying the fresh breeze against her tired face.

“It’s so nice to have a real place to stay again,” she sighs. “I was getting so sick of bedrolls and hard cave floors.”

“Can’t relate,” says Toph. “I love roughing it.” Despite this, she is lounging quite comfortably on one of the beds, her limbs sprawled out, arms folded behind her head. “I guess if it gets you to stop complaining, though, I’m happy Sokka landed us this situation.”

Katara playfully smacks the bedpost. “Oh shut up, Toph. Like you aren’t grateful for the privacy.”

And to illustrate her point, she walks back over to the bed, sliding silkily between Toph’s outstretched legs. Toph immediately curves around her, her chest to Katara’s back, her arms wrapped protectively around her waist.

“Ah, you got me there, babe.” Toph plants a kiss on her shoulder. “When did we last get any quality time together, anyway?”

“Hmm…” Katara rakes her nails down Toph’s thighs, bracketing her in. “There was that one afternoon where Sokka and Aang were both in the village, and we pretty much had the cave to ourselves…”

“I said *quality* time,” Toph gripes. Her hands sink down over the flat of Katara’s stomach. “Any incidents involving drippy caves and voyeuristic lemurs are automatically excluded from that definition.” She slides her fingers down between Katara’s legs, teasing her through the fabric of her clothes. This elicits a short, soft noise just shy of a moan.

“Then - the Earth Kingdom,” Katara breathes, jerking in Toph’s grasp. “Would’ve been - mm - weeks ago.”

Toph can feel the silky, wet heat of Katara’s arousal against her fingers. She gives a tight, clockwise swirl, the kind she knows Katara likes, and smiles when Katara gives a demanding rut against her hand.

When the dust settles, Toph rests her sweaty face on Katara’s bare chest, while Katara runs her fingers through the short, dark strands of Toph’s hair. It’s one of Toph’s favorite feelings in the world. She won’t say that directly, but she sighs with contentment and says, “I know what this reminds me of.”

“Yeah?” asks Katara, raking her nails along Toph’s scalp.

“Hu Xin. Right after that flood.”

It’s a precious and romantic memory, which is maybe why it annoys Toph that Katara outright *snorts*. “This isn’t like that.”

“How not?” Toph asks, clear insult in her tone. Granted, she feels silly, pouting with her face in a pair of magnificent tits.

Toph had known she was attracted to Katara from the moment they first met. Even in that crowded, underground earthbending arena, where the air was thick with the scent of hundreds of people, Katara’s crisp, clean omega scent had stood out. Toph had gotten one whiff and thought, *I* *want that.*

Unfortunately, Toph’s choice of come-on (“You here for an autograph, Sugar?”) earned her a fucking earful. Katara was *not* the type of girl who responded to pigtail-pulling by fretting prettily. She pulled back - hard enough that Toph remembered Aang and Sokka standing in the background of the argument with painfully-clenched teeth.

The first few months after Toph joined up with the group, the two butted heads constantly. Yet judging by that way that crisp, cloying scent would spike whenever she was around, Toph was almost certain Katara secretly liked her back. If only their personalities weren’t so completely incompatible. A very intoxicated Sokka had once complained to Toph that living with the two of them was like being stuck in a box with two feral cats that hated each other, but also desperately wanted to bone.

Hu Xin had been where all of that changed.

Aang and the others were staying in an impoverished little village nestled in the Hu Xin valley, when a terrible monsoon swept in. Occupied by an endless war with the Fire Nation, the Earth Kingdom had little funds to devote to infrastructure. The torrential downpour and rising water levels tested the limits of the long-neglected dam, threatening to flood the valley.

Not wanting to waste a moment, the group split responsibilities. Sokka got the villagers evacuated. Aang was to keep the eastern half of the dam from crumbling under the pressure of wind and water, and Katara and Toph were sent to hold the western half together.

It had been a serious test of their teamwork skills, but there was no time to argue in a life-or-death situation. While howling winds buffeted their bodies and buckets of freezing cold water dumped down from the sky, Katara fought to keep nearly the entire reservoir at bay behind the dam, while Toph was preoccupied molding the earth in an attempt to fix the edifice itself.

She could still remember how Katara had cried out in the middle of bending, howling like she was being beaten from the strain of holding the raging waters back. The sudden torrent of muddy water crashing down the mountainside towards them. The realization that while Katara could just barely keep a tsunami at bay, the sheer mass of the mud was impossible for her to stop. Toph, terrified she was about to listen to the girl she loved get buried alive next to her, widened her stance, focusing with all of her might to deflect that terrible onslaught and save them both.

“Don’t get me wrong - Hu Xin was a big deal,” Katara agrees. The sound of her voice and the soothing stroke to Toph’s hair drags her back to the present, where it’s warm, and dry, and safe. “I think that’s where I really fell in love with you. But it wasn’t like this.”

Katara’s confession sweetens the sting a bit, but Toph still finds herself frowning in reply. “But that’s where we slept together for the first time, right? After the storm cleared up?”

“No way,” Katara insists. “You were afraid to even kiss me properly!”

Suddenly, Toph remembers. The way the cold air bit at their skin even as the rain finally slowed to a trickle. How incredibly quiet it was without the crying of the winds. There had only been the sound of the morning birds and their panting breaths, as they stood side-by-side, utterly spent.

Uncertain, Toph had reached out in Katara’s general direction, looking, even as she felt the fluttering of her heartbeat, for some confirmation that she was alright. Without hesitation, Katara had grabbed that outstretched hand, dragging Toph into an embrace.

“We’re alive,” she’d sobbed.

And as Toph clutched Katara close, she planted a single, embarrassingly chaste kiss on her ear.

Toph feels her skin heat up, twisting her face into Katara’s chest so the other girl won’t tease her for blushing. “Well, you were always telling me how obnoxious I was. I just wanted to be respectful of you for once!”

She feels the ebullience of Katara’s laughter, her head rising and falling with it. “Aw, Toph, you *were* respectful. I thought it was so sweet. Anyway, that wasn’t our first time. That came a few days later, when we got to the next town. Remember? Aang and Sokka were gone for like eight hours, and we found out later it was because they ran into pirates.”

“Oh yeah!” Toph pauses, contemplating. “I was always kinda jealous of that, but - I mean obviously, I had the superior day.”

They laugh, before falling into a contented silence. Even if Katara seemed amused, Toph worries she was being too flippant just now. She hopes that Katara knows she loves her with every ounce of her being. That she would bend endless monsoons if it meant getting to stay with her forever.

Silences alone with Katara are better than any other kind of silence, but Toph cannot be satisfied lying quietly beside even her beloved girlfriend for long.

“Psst, Katara? What’cha thinking about?”

“Aang,” Katara answers.

Toph sits up. “If you’re going to break my heart, can’t you at least choose somebody who’s available?”

“Not like *that*,” Katara huffs, pulling Toph back down to lay on her again. “I’m worried about him.”

“Oh, good.” Toph once again takes her rightful place, her cheek laid against the timpani of Katara’s heart. “What, is it Zuko again?”

“No, not at all, actually. I’m more worried about the White Lotus.”

Sigh. Toph loves her girlfriend to death, but she is a suspicious one. At least she’s gotten off the whole Zuko thing. “Katara, the Lotus are not going to double-cross us. They protected us from the feds, and they’re giving us this awesome place to stay, and they found that tutor for Aang…”

“And that’s all well and good,” Katara concedes, “but I’m worried he’s accruing a debt. What if, in order to make things up to them, they start pulling him into whatever weird agenda they have going here in Kirachu?”

“Katara,” says Toph. “Their political agenda is *our* political agenda.”

“But they mentioned weapons smuggling!” Katara exclaims. “We don’t need to be a part of that!”

“They also don’t want us to just cut and run, so I’m sure they won’t make us do anything we’re not cool with. Look - I know you’re used to us being on the lam, but we’re safe here! We can relax now!”

It was no use. She could feel Katara’s heart quicken against her cheek. “I don’t know, Toph. What about all the men that keep coming through here to meet Aang - isn’t that a problem? If more people know where we’re hiding, doesn’t that mean it’s more likely it could get out? And spirits know Sokka isn’t any help. He adores Master Piandao and would do anything he asked; like yesterday, when he asked if Aang wanted to go on that scouting mission? That was so foolish!”

“But Aang didn’t go along with it, remember?”

“Only because it’d interfere with getting to see Zuko,” Katara mutters.

“So that proves Zuko is a great influence. Listen-” Toph comfortingly pats the boob closest to her face. “I hear you. Let’s not go making enemies with the White Lotus, but I promise next time they ask for something that gives you the heebie jeebies, I’ll back you up. And I’m *sure* if you talk to Aang about it, he’ll hear what you have to say. He really respects your opinion, Katara.”

Finally, Katara’s pulse seems to calm down. “Alright. But I’m holding you to that promise.”
