It barely hurts, but still. Zuko can’t help but sigh to learn that his guilt has been brandished against him once again. At least this is the last time Zhao will ever be able to do this to him.

“I’m surprised you’re asking about any of it,” Azula says. “I wouldn’t think you’d owe those people anything.”

Zuko shrugs, gaze wandering to the hearth. Iroh had left the fire going, and Zuko watches it dance, throwing shadows on the wall. “They were a part of my life for so long. I want to know that they’re all okay. Have you heard anything about Ama?”

He was the person Zuko was most worried about. With Wei imprisoned and his other sons dead, he was lacking a legal guardian. It wouldn’t be easy for him, as an omega, to retain the estate.

Azula shoots her brother a surreptitious look over her third cup of tea. “Have you considered paying Mai and Ty Lee a visit?”

Knowing her, the subject change is deliberate. Zuko plays along. “I haven’t talked to them since they left the capital.”

“You should reach out,” Azula says, conversationally.

“Oh? Are you back in touch?”

Now Azula is the one staring into the hearth, refusing eye contact. “Well. It’s my new lease on life, and whatever. I reached out a while ago to… apologize. And I learned a bit about them.”

“Like what?”

“Mai still teaches, for one. She hates every single one of her students, and would die for them.”

Zuko chuckles. “That sounds like her. What about Ty Lee? How did you find her?”

Azula gives her brother a curious, penetrative look. “She’s with Mai on Shuhon. She has been this whole time.”

“What?” Zuko is crestfallen. As if reading the question right out of his mind, Azula says, “Don’t be mad she never reached out. She had to be careful, with that bastard stalking her the first few months after she left.”

She lifts her nails to inspect them. “Funny thing, though - thanks to that bastard, she’s found another calling. She helps people like her, who have been backed into a corner because of their sex. Last I checked, she has a whole boarding house full of charity cases.”

That’s certainly a revelation. Zuko basks in it, feeling strangely hopeful. “Wow. That’s incredible.”

“It is. You should visit them all someday,” Azula prompts.

But Zuko shakes his head. “We can trade letters, or they can visit me. But I’m never going back to the Fire Nation.”

Maybe it’s a trick of the light, but Azula’s gaze seems to soften. “You know what we’re planning to do, Zuko. Maybe not tomorrow or even next month, but it’s going to be safe again someday. He won’t be there anymore.”

“I’m never going back,” Zuko repeats, voice firm. Azula accepts this with a single, curt nod.

“One last thing,” she says. “I’ve been looking for Mom.”

Zuko can’t bring himself to ask. He watches her for signs of tragedy, but it's impossible to tell. Azula has a perfect poker face.

“...I still haven’t found her,” Azula eventually acquiesces. “But all signs point to her being in the Fire Nation. If she is still alive.”

Zuko can only manage a curt nod. “Well. Maybe when our father is no longer on the throne, she’ll be more willing to show herself.”

The lights of the city outside have all but disappeared, making the window a smear of black on the far wall. Azula stands from the table, pushing her empty cup away. “As delighted as I am to see you, I have been up since before dawn with our allies in the Northern Water Tribe. Considering I’ve made my way to an entirely different continent since then, I’m about to collapse from exhaustion.” She pauses, considering. “And please, ignore my sarcastic tone - it’s purely habit. I *am* delighted to see you.”

Zuko believes her. On impulse, he stands, too, and throws his arms around her. She doesn’t even hesitate to embrace him back. When they pull apart, Zuko takes a moment to appraise her. It’s been years since they’ve been close like this, and she has certainly changed in the meantime. Yet the lack of makeup has her looking like the little sister he remembers.

He looks down, eye caught by a burst of violet. “Are you sure there’s not more to this plan than you’ve been telling me? You’re not trying to unify the Fire Nation with our new allies to the north?”

Azula blinks, confused. “What? No. Why?”

“...You have a hickey.”

Going scarlet, Azula immediately slaps a palm over it. “Good *night* ,” she says, and begins stalking towards the back room. Zuko cranes his neck to watch her, calling out, “Will you two be co-ruling both countries together, or will you rule your own territories separately? What do *those* treaties look like? Does her father know!”

“Shut up!” Azula hisses, before slamming the door shut behind her. Somewhere in the back room, a baby cries. Zuko rushes off to check on her, still wiping tears of laughter from his eyes.

---

Zuko doesn’t know any of his mother’s recipes. What he does know are the little campfire meals he had to learn on the road, and he expands on these, with Aang’s help, to a range of vegetarian dishes, and a Southern Water Tribe recipe Katara showed him that they’ve had to adapt for the sorts of tubers that grow in these warmer climates. Zuko is not good at cooking, but he isn’t bad, and besides, it’s something can do with his fire that heals more than hurts. So he takes that heat and he bakes and he bakes and he bakes, filling Izumi’s stomach with the sorts of sweet, self-made treasures a distinguished omega of the Fire Nation court would be scorned for making. And she gobbles them all up like they are the finest the world could offer, because they are the finest her world has offered.

For the last few days, Ba Sing Se has been abuzz with an energy unlike anything Zuko has seen in the years since moving here. It started with a rumor that a mass of Earth Kingdom troops would soon be coming home, then burst into full-fledged fervor when the first of them breached the walls with the news: the stalemate was finally over. The *war* was finally over.

Which is why Zuko is spending all of his time furiously cooking - to distract himself. His eyes keep straying to the window, watching the road for signs of Aang. Every time he doesn’t see him, he grows nervous, until he reminds himself of the joy spreading through Ba Sing Se.

(Ugly thoughts try to remind him this isn’t a city built on truths - but the gates have been open for *years* now. Surely they couldn’t get away with a lie like this one?)

Zuko has made the mistake of choosing a dish that simmers low and long, and Izumi is simply too perfect a toddler, content drawing pictures of her extensive inner world at the table, which means Zuko’s mind is free to wander. He finds himself thinking about the last time he saw Aang before he left for the Fire Nation. It was here, in this same kitchen.

Aang had leaned against the counter closest to the door and heaved an exhausted sigh. “Your sister’s not as forgiving a tutor as you were!”

“No surprise there. But you should listen to her. She knows her stuff,” Zuko replied. He drifted over to Aang and dropped a dumpling into his hand. “Try this one.”

“Yeah, I know, just. I still think what you taught me was enough. I don’t need lightning bending, or blue fire, or any of this… extra deadly stuff.” Aang paused to pop the dumpling in his mouth, humming with approval as he chewed.

“Good?”

“Vrry gd.” Aang swallowed. “Your best yet!”

“Thanks. I added bamboo shoots like you asked.”

It had been easy enough then to ignore the looming fear of all that Aang was preparing for, and instead focus on spooning the filling into the dough. Zuko remembers Aang folding dumplings alongside him, their silence companionable.

Until Aang had broken it. “Zuko… are you sure you’re okay with this? We’ve built a whole life together. If I go back to the Fire Nation to face him, it’s possible that I’ll…”

Those gray eyes were troubled. Zuko had to resist the inborn urge to chase those storm clouds away by insisting everything was fine.

“Of course I want to keep you here,” Zuko said. “But that wouldn’t be fair to you, and it wouldn’t be fair to everyone counting on you. I accept that my feelings are less important than the fate of the world.”

“Zuko…”

“I trust you to come back,” Zuko said stiffly, once again wrapping and pinching dough, all the while fighting away the tears that nipped at the corners of his eyes. “And I know… I know if you don’t come back, it won’t be because you didn’t want to.”

He’d wrapped about three more dumplings before Aang spoke again. “I wish I could do more for you in return.”

“In return for what?”

“Leaving you here.”

Zuko’s hands were caked in wet flour - an abhorrent texture - so he used his wrist to scrub at his eyes. “You’re saving the world. You’re already doing enough.”

“Still. I could do more to bring you justice. Your father…”

“I won’t have you going against your beliefs for me, either, Aang,” Zuko replied. “If in all your soul searching, you’ve finally found another way to resolve it, then by all means. Don’t feel you have to change on my behalf.”

Aang’s fingers started to move again, folding dough over filling, pinching the corners. There’d been a learning curve where his movements in the kitchen had always seemed more assured than Zuko’s. Now it was the reverse.

“Katara doesn’t have the same reservations,” Aang said, softly. “Nor Azula.”

And because Zuko couldn’t bear to believe he was worth a gesture, he started to feel guilty. “Isn’t that the same as going against your beliefs? Turning a blind eye as others do it for you?”

Aang shook his head. “I cannot dictate for them what they should do. If they’re going to respect my convictions, then I am going to respect theirs.”

Still, he abandoned a malformed dumpling at the corner of his cutting board, both hands gripping the counter as he slumped. “I never wanted to be a general, Zuko. But if Azula’s coup doesn’t pan out, I’ll have to march an army into the Fire Nation capital.”

“You won’t *have* to.”

“I owe everyone that much and more for running away in the first place.”

Zuko remembers running his hands over those shoulders, chi following the path of his palms down Aang’s back. Standing with hands clasped to watch the window. Had Aang seen the world beyond, begging him to save it, or had he been able to appreciate the image right outside the window, of the city where they’d made a home?

Zuko is yanked from his reveries all at once by a delighted shriek, then the scrape of a stool being pushed back from the counter as Izumi rushes to the back door.

“Be careful,” Zuko starts to say, but as he follows her into the back room, he is stopped silent by the sight of Aang, as whole as he was the day he left. He smiles down at their daughter as she leaps around his legs, little arms straining for him to pick her up. He slips his sandals off, arranging them just off the side of the door before he gathers Izumi up into his arms for a hug.

“I didn’t see you on the road,” Zuko says numbly. One corner of Aang’s mouth lifts, and there it is, for the first time in what feels like a millenia: that lopsided smile Zuko loves so dearly.

“I took the side road,” Aang says. “It’s faster.”

It’s like he has only been gone a few days, except his loss still lingers in Zuko’s heart, as painful as those first hours following a burn. At least now it can begin to heal.

“Is it really over?” Zuko asks, fear creeping into his voice.

Over Izumi’s shoulder, Aang nods. “Azula’s the Fire Lord. The followers she’s gained in the court and the Northern Water Tribe ships sitting in the capital harbor made sure of that.”

“And my father?”

“He’ll never hurt you again.”

Zuko steps forward, wrapping his arms around Aang and Izumi both. He holds them both tightly enough that he hopes to anchor them here, with him, for the rest of their lives. They grip him just as tightly back.

---

A crowd of loved ones barrels through the house to celebrate Aang’s return. Hours later, Zuko and Aang stand alone amongst the refuse - mostly gifts of food, peeled fruit and baked things, but there are scuff marks on the floor and chairs still pulled back from tables to signal they were here. The couple is shell-shocked with the extent of everyone’s warmth and love. Izumi is barely able to lift her head from Aang’s shoulder; she tries valiantly to maximize her precious time with her father, but sleep claims her, so they put her to bed.

Zuko has only barely pressed the door shut, has only just heard the *click* of the lock in its place when he finds himself being swept up into the air, and he laughs and holds on tight as Aang twirls him in a thousand circles. When he lands, the world swirls in a drunken blur all around him, and Aang is the only thing that’s clear. Zuko holds onto Aang, fingers braced against the barest stubble on the back of his neck as he leans up and kisses him. Aang receives him gladly, fisting Zuko’s shorn locks in order to pull his head back and deepen the kiss.

They’ve spent so much time apart. They should savor the moment, but they still feel the urgency of an impending loss, even though it’s finally over, even though they get to just be. So they have trouble taking their time at first, unwilling to waste a single moment, clothes falling where they land. They will have to tidy up before morning, or risk a thousand questions from Izumi. At the very least, when they retreat to their bedroom, they shut the door as quietly as possible behind them.

When they finally break that kiss - that endless, almost brutal kiss, mouths desperate to make up for lost time - Zuko rasps, “Don’t you ever leave me again.”

“Never,” Aang agrees, words hot against the skin of Zuko’s neck, chased by a tongue, by teeth.

Zuko shivers in his arms, arches against the hand that clutches his hip. “I mean it. I’ll tie you down if I have to.”

That earns him a squeeze of the ass, a bite at the sensitive skin just below his undamaged ear. “ *There’s* a thought.”

Zuko’s breath hitches. “You want to?”

He can *hear* the twinkle in Aang’s eye. “I want to prove I’m here for good. What better way to convince you than submit to your whims?”

Then it’s a mad dash around the room to find something they can use. Rummaging in a drawer, Aang finds the old academy uniform headband he’d used when hiding in Kirachu. Zuko gives a bark of a laugh when he sees it - it’s too good not to use.

Zuko sits on Aang’s abdomen as he ties his wrists to the headboard, careful to ask what’s comfortable, careful not to cut off circulation. When he’s finished, he stretches out over Aang, presses their clothed laps together as he kisses him.

“You want to be on top?” Aang breathes between kisses, and Zuko hums, says, “I *am* on top,” before kissing Aang’s smiling lips.

“You know what I mean.”

“Later,” Zuko murmurs, running his lips along Aang’s neck. “I’ve missed having you inside me.”

He takes his time. He slides down Aang’s body, using cheek and lips to torture Aang’s erection through his pants. Zuko delights in the blush that spreads over Aang’s ears, the futile tug at his bindings. Zuko slowly drags his pants over his hips, Aang’s erection springing up once it’s freed.

“Ties still comfortable?”

“All green,” Aang confirms. Zuko smiles, taking Aang’s cock in hand. He pauses to appreciate how swollen and ruddy the head already is before he leans in to take it into his mouth, to swirl his tongue over the ridges, to dip into the slit.

Aang lets out a long, low moan that sounds like a sigh of relief. His entire body seems to languish, to relax under Zuko’s ministrations. Zuko’s tongue moves with every dip of his head, lavishing Aang’s cock with attention. He can taste the precum gathering, relishes the chance to pull back, to lick and kiss at the head until he can feel one of Aang’s legs that he’s braced against start to tremble.

Zuko gives Aang’s cock one last lick, from root to tip, before he pulls back and begins to undress himself. There’s a laugh in Aang’s groan of disappointment, and he watches, smiling with blurry eyes as Zuko removes the last of his layers, straddles his lap. Pleasuring Aang has already got him aroused, but he makes a show of biting his lip and stroking himself, pleased at the clarity that rushes into Aang’s pleasure-soft gaze, how he can’t seem to tear his eyes off Zuko.

When he finally takes Aang in hand and begins to open himself up, Aang’s breath quickens, the headband pulled taught against the headboard. The desperation is part of the fun, and he hasn’t asked to be let free, but Zuko wants those long-fingered hands on him, so as he sinks down, he bends over, plucks at the knot.

Aang rushes to fill the space, hips surging upwards into that tight, wet heat, arms flying up to ensnare Zuko in his grasp. They fuck with their arms wrapped up around each other, faces inches away, not kissing or purring sweet nothings, but simply breathing one another’s air. As he rides Aang, as Aang thrusts up inside him, as those many neglected, sensitive nerves are stimulated over and over, Zuko feels as though he can feel it in their mingled breaths, that spark of chi, that soul-deep connection.

They breathe in sync, those fires in their bellies roiling low, building to a climax, sending them trembling as they come clutching one another. Zuko can feel the burst of wetness inside him at exactly the moment he comes in Aang’s fist, and he rolls his hips in a few last, torturous movements exactly as Aang gives him a few last, torturous strokes.

They do not crumble into the sheets, but stay there upright, holding one another. The room is silent except for the percussive sounds of their breathing.

Then Aang reaches up. Gently pulls Zuko’s face to kiss his lips. The scar. The burned, shapeless remnant of an ear.

“I love you, Zuko,” he murmurs. Zuko takes Aang’s hand in his, kissing his fingers.

“Love you, Aang.”

The End

### End Notes

#### Chapter End Notes

Thank you enormously to everyone who read this fic. Your thoughts and feedback meant the world to me. You’ve all done wonders for my self esteem as a writer, and kept me going through some seriously difficult periods of my life.

While I’ve had a relatively clear vision of this story’s ending from the get-go, there are still things that naturally changed along the way as the story developed beyond what my outlines could have predicted. If you’re interested, read on to learn how the ending changed!

1&#46; Zuko was originally going to give into his desire to pursue Aang only after the realization that Zhao was already embroiled in an extramarital affair. There was going to be this moment where Zuko found out, and was just stunned silent with rage, because he’d let Zhao do so much to him, had weathered so much violence at his hands without complaint, and it still hadn’t been enough to satisfy him. But I hadn’t thought of how unbelievable this realization would be after the burning of the Lesser Hall; Zhao was just so incredibly irredeemable then, even in the eyes of someone who had trauma-bonded with him.

2&#46; There were going to be Real miscarriages, but Zuko was always going to end the series with a successful birth. In the end, going back and forth and ending with the same result just seemed unnecessary, so I went for a quick fake-out instead. I was desperate to keep Sonzehn’s cameo because I wanted these final chapters to encapsulate the people, even veritable strangers, who cared about Zuko’s well-being enough to extend a helping hand.

3&#46; (Zuko’s pregnancy journey is NOT meant to be a message about how all pregnancies should have to come to term, because actually, I believe anyone should be able to end a pregnancy for any reason at all! It’s just that as a person with one very loving and one very cruel parent, who doesn’t want to be stuck with his abusive partner but also wants a chance at a family with another partner who cannot get him pregnant, Zuko is understandably going to have a lot of really complicated feelings about pregnancy.)

4&#46; For a long time, I pictured Zuko’s reunion with Aang in Ba Sing Se being the end of it. Hug, cue curtains. No real scenes with Izumi. As all the subplots blew up, I realized I owed everyone a more comprehensive wrap-up than that.

5&#46; Zhao was always going to be maimed in the Agni Kai, to parallel the injury he gave Zuko. But he wasn’t always going to die in that battle! Instead, he was going to be banished to the South Pole. For a long time I planned an epilogue where this southern water tribe kid was freaking out seeing this scary man just wandering around on the tundra, and his mother’s anxiety that the Fire Nation had somehow returned to the south pole. Ultimately Zhao’s hubris would lead him to believe he could survive out on the tundra by himself, and he would die of hypothermia. I held onto this idea for a long time, and it was really hard to let it go, but I just didn’t think it made sense or gave the story any closure!! (and it would probably be another 9,000 words I just cannot write)

6&#46; Once I let go of the banishment to the South Pole, I toyed with other ways of leaving Zhao alive, e.g., rotting in the dungeons of Caldera. but it made me very nervous to picture him just… getting to stay alive past the ending, even if he would never escape. I just thought that’d plague Zuko for the rest of his life. I guess Azula could’ve killed him when she took over - but would an off-screen death be remotely satisfying? I also didn't want Zuko to kill Zhao himself. that just felt very against Zuko’s character, both in this fic and in canon.

7&#46; Piandao almost lived. As in, I almost implied Wei helped him escape his execution, and revealed him in this chapter. But Piandao’s presence distracted from the more important character threads and started to balloon the chapter. So I decided to keep him dead. He was so minor to this fic anyway, I didn’t think his survival would change anyone’s opinion of the ending. So… sorry, Piandao. ^^;

I will miss this fic, but I’m also really excited to embark on the next stage of my writing journey. I’m hoping to do original stuff from here on out, but who knows. I may eventually write fic again. Regardless, thank you all for reading :)
